arxiv-1803-09090.title: Physical Layer Security in the Presence of Interference
arxiv-1803-09090.creator: Dimitrios S. Karas, Alexandros-Apostolos A. Boulogeorgos, George K. Karagiannidis, Arumugam Nallanathan
arxiv-1803-09090.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Dimitrios S. Karas, Alexandros-Apostolos A. Boulogeorgos, George K. Karagiannidis, Arumugam Nallanathan. We evaluate and quantify the joint effect of fading and multiple interferers on the physical-layer (PHY) security of a system consisted of a base-station (BS), a legitimate user, and an eavesdropper.

arxiv-2105-09298.title: Distributed algorithms for the least square solution of linear equations
arxiv-2105-09298.creator: Yi Huang, Ziyang Meng
arxiv-2105-09298.description: Abstract This paper proposes distributed algorithms for solving linear equations to seek a least square solution via multi-agent networks. We consider that each agent has only access to a small and imcomplete block of linear equations rather than the complete row or column in the existing literatures. Firstly, we focus on the case of a homogeneous partition of linear equations.

arxiv-2112-06053.title: FedSoft: Soft Clustered Federated Learning with Proximal Local Updating
arxiv-2112-06053.creator: Yichen Ruan, Carlee Joe-Wong
arxiv-2112-06053.description: Abstract Traditionally, clustered federated learning groups clients with the same data distribution into a cluster, so that every client is uniquely associated with one data distribution and helps train a model for this distribution. We relax this hard association assumption to soft clustered federated learning, which allows every local dataset to follow a mixture of multiple source distributions.

arxiv-2203-15874.title: Temperature-Aware Monolithic 3D DNN Accelerators for Biomedical Applications
arxiv-2203-15874.creator: Prachi Shukla, Vasilis F. Pavlidis, Emre Salman, Ayse K. Coskun
arxiv-2203-15874.description: Abstract In this paper, we focus on temperature-aware Monolithic 3D ( Mono3D ) deep neural network (DNN) inference accelerators for biomedical applications. We develop an optimizer that tunes aspect ratios and footprint of the accelerator under user-defined performance and thermal constraints, and generates near-optimal configurations.

arxiv-2301-00040.title: Optimization-based Sensitivity Analysis for Unmeasured Confounding using Partial Correlations Thanks: QZ is partly supported by the EPSRC grant EP/V049968/1.
arxiv-2301-00040.creator: Tobias Freidling
arxiv-2301-00040.description: Abstract Causal inference necessarily relies upon untestable assumptions; hence, it is crucial to assess the robustness of obtained results to violations of identification assumptions. However, such sensitivity analysis is only occasionally undertaken in practice, as many existing methods require analytically tractable solutions and their results are often difficult to interpret.

arxiv-2508-03802.title: Geometric fragmentation and anomalous thermalization in cubic dimer model
arxiv-2508-03802.creator: Joel Steinegger, Debasish Banerjee, Emilie Huffman, Lukas Rammelmüller
arxiv-2508-03802.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joel Steinegger, Debasish Banerjee, Emilie Huffman, Lukas Rammelmüller. While quantum statistical mechanics triumphs in explaining many equilibrium phenomena, there is an increasing focus on going beyond conventional scenarios of thermalization. Traditionally examples of non-thermalizing systems are either integrable, or disordered. Recently, examples of translationally-invariant physical systems have been discovered whose excited energies avoid thermalization either due to local constraints (whether exact or emergent), or due to higher-form symmetries.

pmc-11518540.creator: A Baran, M Sülü, C Kekilli, A Avcu, S Gündoğdu, G Boz, M Genç
pmc-11518540.description: BackgroundUniversity students turn to addictive substances to cope with the anxiety and stress caused by separation from family, adaptation to a new environment, as well as many economic and social problems. This study aimed to examine smoking, alcohol, substance, technology, and gambling addiction among university students.MethodsThe data of this cross-sectional study were collected between February and March 2024.

pmc-11672611.title: Identification of Factors Determining Patterns of Serum C-Reactive Protein Level Reduction in Response to Treatment Initiation in Patients with Drug-Susceptible Pulmonary Tuberculosis
pmc-11672611.creator: Agnija Kivrane, Viktorija Ulanova, Solveiga Grinberga, Eduards Sevostjanovs, Anda Viksna, Iveta Ozere, Ineta Bogdanova, Ilze Simanovica, Inga Norvaisa, Leonora Pahirko, Dace Bandere, Renate Ranka, Fabrizio Palmieri, Gina Gualano, Francesco Di Gennaro
pmc-11672611.description: Background: Serum C-reactive protein (CRP) levels vary depending on radiological and bacteriological findings at the time of tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis. However, the utility of this biomarker in monitoring response to anti-TB treatment and identifying patients at risk of treatment failure is not well established.

pmc-13334678.title: An Activity‐Dependent NEPAS–PTX3 Axis Links Neurovascular and Myelin Deficits to Cognitive Impairment
pmc-13334678.creator: Boya Hu, Zifei Chen, Bingmei Sun, Jiale Gao, Jiale Xu, Xiaochun Guo, Fenfei Gao, Zhongsi Wang, Jie Wu, Xiaoyu Ji, Peipei Liu, Bing Huang
pmc-13334678.description: Acquired cognitive impairments occur in diverse neurological and psychiatric conditions, yet the mechanisms linking neural circuit activity to neurovascular function remain poorly understood. Using a mouse model of nicotine withdrawal (WD), we identified an activity‐dependent NEPAS–pentraxin‐3 (PTX3) axis in mPFC neurons that couples circuit hypoactivity to cognitive deficits.

pmc-13671357.title: Human erythroid models of sickle cell disease
pmc-13671357.creator: Deborah E. Daniels, Maria A. Lizarralde‐Iragorri, Fatima O. Oyawoye, David C. Rees, Jan Frayne, Sara El Hoss
pmc-13671357.description: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a group of severe inherited red blood cell disorders causing a major global healthcare burden. Despite recent advances in gene therapy and stem cell transplantation, treatment options remain very limited, highlighting the urgent need for the development of new therapeutic approaches.
